roleLabel: One of the first social communicators of Riacho He Hé
summary: Norma Edith Bedoya, known to everyone as Norma de Vargas, was born on 19 January 1955 in the city of Formosa. She spent much of her life recording and sharing the reality of Riacho He Hé.
openingTitle:
A woman who
told the story
of her town.
paragraphs: Journalist, correspondent, photographer and newspaper distributor. Bringing the news to the town was part of the same craft.

chapters.title: Pioneer of communication
paragraphs: Her work as a journalist, correspondent and photographer meant that the facts, the voices and the people of Riacho He Hé remained on the pages of the press and in the town's memory.

Delivering newspapers and magazines was the other half of that task: bringing information to where people live. In her youth she lived for thirteen years in Buenos Aires and trained in photography. Julio César Duarte, director of the magazine Protagonistas, gave her her first camera.

chapters.title:
The news
that told
a town
paragraphs: For years she was a correspondent for Diario La Mañana. Public works, institutions, anniversaries and everyday life in Riacho He Hé found a place in a provincial newspaper.
On 24 June 2007 the paper published a special for the town's 98th anniversary. Those pages are part of the archive of how the town saw itself.

photos.alt: Inside page of Diario La Mañana from 24 June 2007. The headline reads Riacho He Hé, a town of landscape and warmth, next to a note on the municipal government and anniversary notices.
photos.caption: Diario La Mañana special, 24 June 2007, for the 98th anniversary of Riacho He Hé.

chapters.title:
Behind every story
there was a life.
paragraphs: She walked streets, institutions, schools and rural settlements. Camera and notebook were the tools of a craft with no timetable: when something had to be covered, she had to be there.

chapters.title:
The photograph
that made history
paragraphs: When the Obelisk of Riacho He Hé was inaugurated, Norma wanted an image that would show the scale of the work. Her husband, Daniel Vargas, went up in the municipal lift to take the aerial shot.
That photograph is part of the town's visual archive. Behind it was the work the two of them shared.

photos.alt: Aerial view of the Riacho He Hé Obelisk. The white monument is seen from above, with the town coat of arms and name on the base, a tiled path, and three men standing to one side.
photos.caption: Photograph taken to document the inauguration of the Riacho He Hé Obelisk.

photos.alt: A man in the basket of a municipal cherry picker, raised above the street. Another man stands on the truck step. Cars and a line of trees in the background.
photos.caption: Daniel Vargas during the taking of the panoramic photograph of the Obelisk.

chapters.title:
She did not only tell
the community.
She also built it.
paragraphs: She sat on the Founding Committee of the Public Library of Riacho He Hé, today the Don Félix Atilio Cabrera Popular Public Library. On the plaque placed on 24 June 1996 she appears as Norma Bedoya de Vargas, deputy treasurer.

She had earlier been part of the first Committee of the Mothers' League. In the book her words remain: “It is not to give myself credit; it only speaks of a just time when everything still had to be done and I was one part of that building.”

photos.alt: Front of the Don Félix Atilio Cabrera Popular Public Library: a cream building with a tiled roof, a black gate and a plaque on the wall naming the library and the year 1990.
photos.caption: Don Félix Atilio Cabrera Popular Public Library, Riacho He Hé.

photos.alt: Copper plaque of the Founding Committee of the Public Library of Riacho He Hé, dated 10 September 1993. In the list, Norma Bedoya de Vargas appears as deputy treasurer.
photos.caption: Founding Committee plaque. Norma Bedoya de Vargas appears as deputy treasurer.

chapters.title:
Her town
recognised her too.
paragraphs: Neighbours made her a welcome banner as correspondent for Diario La Mañana. It remains as an archive piece: recognition from a town, not a corporate award.

photos.alt: Handmade yellow banner: Welcome Norma B Vargas correspondent Diario La Mañana Riacho He Hé.
photos.caption: Welcome banner that the neighbours of Riacho He Hé made for her as correspondent for Diario La Mañana.

chapters.title:
The woman
behind the journalist
paragraphs: Behind every assignment there was a daughter, a mother, a companion. She was the daughter of Francisco Antonio Bedoya and Luisa Caballero.
Those who knew her well remember the generosity and the everyday commitment, not only the craft.

photos.alt: Norma, in a yellow floral blouse, with her mother, Luisa Caballero, who is smiling in a red dress with white dots. They are inside a house.
photos.caption: Norma with her mother, Luisa Caballero.

chapters.title:
Family,
her greatest treasure
paragraphs: She came to Riacho He Hé with her husband, Daniel Vargas. They had two sons, Miguel and Luis, and six grandchildren.
After every story, every assignment and every working day, she came back to that place.

photos.alt: Black-and-white photograph from their youth: Norma de Vargas, in a dark pinafore and a light blouse, with Daniel Vargas on a stone staircase.
photos.caption: Norma and Daniel Vargas, a photograph from their youth.

quotes.quote: Norma was a woman ahead of her time. Her commitment to communication and to the growth of Riacho He-Hé left an indelible mark on our community.
quotes.author: Celina Espíndola

quotes.quote: To speak of Norma Bedoya is to speak of the first steps of local journalism and of a woman who made communication a true life's work.
quotes.author: Cristian Alejandro Cabrera

quotes.quote: She taught me that to communicate was not only to speak. It was to listen. It was to observe. It was to understand the other person.
quotes.author: Miguel Vargas

bridge.title: More than a house
paragraphs: Telling the story of a community is also a way of building it. That is what Norma did all her life.

The intention of this project is that that legacy can inspire new opportunities for other people from Riacho He Hé. First, rebuild a house. There is not yet a constituted organisation, and no published programme.

book.title: Norma Edith Bedoya (Norma de Vargas)
book.subtitle: Pioneer of communication in Riacho He-Hé
book.author: Griselda Fernández
book.lead: A commemorative work from 2026. It gathers testimonies, documents and photographs of her path.

cover.alt: Cover of the book Norma Edith Bedoya (Norma de Vargas), Pioneer of communication in Riacho He-Hé. A portrait of Norma appears next to the Obelisk, the Public Library and a Diario La Mañana front page.
cover.caption: Cover of the 2026 commemorative work.

portrait.alt: Norma looks at the camera, smiling slightly. She is in her kitchen, wearing a black blouse with white dots. Behind her, a cupboard with glasses and a shelf of framed family photographs.

photos.alt: A close portrait of Norma. She wears a light-blue and blue striped shirt and looks at the camera with a contained smile.
Norma standing in the kitchen in a fuchsia blouse printed with flowers. Beside her, a vase with an open pink flower.
